title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Billing Manual: Billing Units of a Sensor Refill Drawn on the Newest Written Order
content:
## Reimbursement and Billing Manual — Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program

### Sensor refill units (A4239) drawn on the authorization grant of the newest written order

Larkfield's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program counts here the billing units of a sensor refill (A4239) on a tier where each refill requires the customer's own confirmation — the CGM Commercial HMO Program, CGM Commercial PPO Program, CGM Medicare Advantage Program, CGM Original Medicare Program and CGM Medicaid Program — that draws on the authorization grant resting on the newest written order of the item. The count is made as follows.

1. The delivery. The next delivery draws on the authorization grant resting on the newest written order of the item: the newest written order is the item's written order with the latest order date, and the grant drawn is the authorization grant of the item recorded as based on that order (where more than one is, the one with the latest valid-through date). The delivery carries the fewest of three counts of 30-day blocks:
   - the 30-day blocks of one standard shipment, that is the tier's standard days of supply per refill shipment divided by 30;
   - the whole 30-day blocks from today through that grant's valid-through date, both days counted (the calendar days from today through the valid-through date, today and that date included, divided by 30, dropping any remainder; none once the valid-through date is past);
   - the blocks the program's units still authorized to ship allow at the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply (those units divided by that allowance, dropping any remainder; none when no units remain).
   With no such grant the delivery carries nothing. The delivery's units are its blocks multiplied by the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply.
2. The latest refill and the paid-supply end. The latest refill is the item's refill shipment with the latest ship date, read for its ship date, its supply days, its billing route and the claim submitted for it (the latest claim submitted for that shipment). Its supply counts as paid by the payer for its supply days when it was billed by payer claim, from its ship date; its paid supply days are then its supply days, and a latest refill billed in any other way carries no paid supply days. The paid-supply end is the latest refill's ship date plus those paid supply days, counted in calendar days.
3. The payer authorization. The payer authorization is the grant the latest refill drew on. Its units left are the units that grant credits less the units of every refill shipment drawn on it, never below zero.
4. Units beyond the payer authorization. When the delivery draws on a grant other than the one the latest refill drew on, the units beyond the payer authorization are the delivery's units less the payer authorization's units left, never below zero; when the delivery draws on that same grant there are none.
5. The pump delivery and the over-limit justification. The pump delivery is the pump delivery date recorded on the customer's Insulin Pump Program. The over-limit justification is the latest medical record on the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment whose purpose is over-limit justification, dated by the practitioner visit it records.
6. The past-due amount. Let the hold months be the tier's past-due age in days divided by 30, rounded down to a whole number of months. The past-due amount is the total of the remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and patient refunds posted on the program, less those of them posted fewer than the hold months, in whole calendar months, before today (that is, a posting whose whole calendar months from its posting date to today are fewer than the hold months), less every patient payment and balance adjustment posted on the program, whatever its date.
7. The amount an approved payment plan covers. When the program has an approved payment plan, let the plan months be the whole calendar months from the day the latest approved plan was logged to today. The plan's installments are current when the program's patient payments posted fewer whole calendar months before today than one more than the plan months reach, in total, the plan's monthly amount multiplied by the plan months. While they are current, the plan covers the past-due remittance patient responsibility left after those credits, other than the posting named on the latest hardship application: the remittance patient responsibility posted the hold months or more before today, less every patient payment and balance adjustment posted on the program, less the amount of the posting named on the latest hardship application on the program, never below zero. With no approved plan, or while its installments are not current, the plan covers nothing.
8. The earliest permitted ship date. The earliest permitted ship date is the tier's refill ship lead days, counted in calendar days, before the latest refill's ship date plus its supply days.
9. Units at risk. When the paid-supply end is after today, every 30-day block of the delivery is at risk; when the paid-supply end is today or earlier, no block is at risk. The units at risk are the at-risk blocks multiplied by the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply.
10. The ship-time test. The uncovered past-due amount is the past-due amount less the covered amount, never below zero, and zero on a tier whose past-due age is 0. The delivery ships today only when its earliest permitted ship date is not after today and the uncovered past-due amount is below the tier's past-due hold minimum, or the tier's past-due age is 0.
11. Exposed units and the waiting rule. The exposed units are the units at risk together with the units beyond the payer authorization. The delivery ships in full, all of its units, when it has no exposed units, and otherwise waits.
12. The units shipped. Each adjustment to this count changes the shipment so worked out as that adjustment states, in this order: the earliest ship date and the paid-supply end are moved or replaced first, the at-risk blocks are then marked against the paid-supply end as moved, blocks are then taken off those at-risk blocks, and the waiting rule is replaced last. The refill ships a whole number of units, never below zero, and nothing when the delivery cannot ship today.

Whole calendar months from one date to a later date are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier than the earlier date's calendar day.

### Quantities and the records they rest on

| Quantity | Read from |
|---|---|
| Newest written order and its date | the item's written orders on the program, by order date |
| Grant drawn and its valid-through date | the item's authorization grants recorded as based on that order |
| Units still authorized to ship | the program record |
| Latest refill: ship date, supply days, billing route, claim, grant drawn | the item's refill shipments, by ship date, and the claim submitted for that shipment |
| Payer authorization's units left | the units that grant credits and the refill shipments drawn on it |
| Pump delivery | the pump delivery date on the customer's Insulin Pump Program |
| Over-limit justification | the CGM program's medical records with purpose over-limit justification, by visit date |
| Past-due amount | remittances, patient charges, refunds, payments and balance adjustments on the program's billing ledger |
| Plan coverage | the program's approved payment plan request (logged date, monthly amount), its payments, and the posting named on the latest hardship application |
| Tier figures | the tier's standard days of supply per refill shipment, sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply, refill ship lead days, past-due age in days and past-due hold minimum, as the program's tier tables state them |

### Worked example (hypothetical figures throughout)

Suppose a tier's figures were a standard shipment of 60 days, 2 units per 30 days of supply, refill ship lead days of 5, a past-due age of 60 days and a past-due hold minimum of 40.00 USD; these are illustrative only. Today is a hypothetical 1 March. The grant resting on the newest written order is valid through 31 May, and 10 units are still authorized to ship.

- Blocks: one standard shipment gives 2 blocks; 1 March through 31 May, both days counted, is 92 days, 3 whole blocks; 10 units at 2 per block allow 5 blocks. The fewest is 2 blocks, so the delivery is 4 units.
- The latest refill shipped on 15 January with 30 days of supply, billed by payer claim: its paid-supply end is 15 January plus 30 days, 14 February, which is not after 1 March, so no block is at risk. Its earliest permitted ship date is 5 days before 14 February, 9 February, which is not after today.
- Case A: the latest refill drew on the same grant as the delivery. No units are beyond the payer authorization, nothing is exposed, and the delivery's 4 units ship in full.
- Case B: the latest refill drew on an older grant with 3 units left. The delivery's 4 units exceed them by 1, one unit is exposed, and the delivery waits.
- Past-due: the hold months are 2. A remittance patient responsibility of 120.00 posted on a hypothetical 10 November of the year before is 3 whole months old and counts; a patient charge of 20.00 posted on 20 February is 0 whole months old and is left out; patient payments total 50.00. The past-due amount is 70.00, not below 40.00, so with no approved plan the refill ships nothing today. Had a plan with a monthly amount of 25.00 been logged on 5 January (plan months 1) with a 50.00 payment posted on 10 January (1 whole month old, fewer than 2), the installments are current, the plan covers 120.00 less 50.00, that is 70.00, the uncovered amount is zero, and in Case A the 4 units ship.

### Points of judgement

- The supply drawn and the supply already paid are read from different grants when the latest refill drew on an older grant; the units left on that older grant decide how many of the delivery's units lie beyond it.
- Under clause 11 a delivery with any exposed unit waits.
- Payments and balance adjustments are credited whatever their posting date, while charges, refunds and remittance patient responsibility count only once they are the hold months old.
